Fully Managed or Limited Management

Two ways to let your property. The difference is who makes the repair decisions, so choose the level of involvement that suits you.

The two plans

Fully Managed

Hand over full control

Lowest landlord involvement
  • You hand over full control of day-to-day management
  • GETLET orders repairs directly without prior approval, within written delegated authority
  • Gas and electrical certification arranged through GETLET's agencies
  • Tenant issues handled end to end
  • Costs deducted from rent via PayProp

Contact us for pricing

Request a written quotation
Limited Management

Keep the decision rights

Higher landlord involvement
  • You keep the decision rights on repairs and spending
  • GETLET asks first; work starts only after you give permission
  • Certification is arranged once you approve
  • GETLET reports tenant issues, gets your approval, then dispatches
  • Approved costs deducted via PayProp

The detail that matters

"No prior approval" never means unlimited spending

Each plan has limits that are agreed in writing. These are set out in your management agreement.

Fully Managed: agreed limits

Spending ceiling
A spending ceiling is agreed in writing. Routine repairs up to that ceiling are ordered without asking you first.
Reserve
Any rent reserve held back for repairs is agreed in writing and shown on every statement.
Major works rule
Major works above the ceiling are never ordered without your approval, except to make a property safe.

Limited Management: approval process

Approval channel
We ask for your approval by your preferred contact route, and record your answer against the job.
Landlord response window
A response window for each type of job is agreed in your management agreement.
If there is no reply
If we do not hear back, we chase you and escalate. Work other than making a property safe does not start without your permission.

Be aware: in Limited Management, your approval is an extra dependency for repair timing. The quicker you reply, the quicker the work can start. We explain this openly so there are no surprises.

How we handle one repair

Example: a boiler fault, step by step

An illustrative scenario showing how the same problem moves through each plan.

Fully Managed

  1. Tenant reports the boiler has stopped working.
  2. GETLET checks the property is on Fully Managed.
  3. A heating contractor is booked directly, within the agreed authority.
  4. Contractor attends and repairs or advises.
  5. The invoice is entered in PayProp and deducted from the next rent.
  6. You see it on your statement with the invoice behind it.

Limited Management

  1. Tenant reports the boiler has stopped working.
  2. GETLET checks the property is on Limited Management.
  3. GETLET contacts you with the issue and an estimate, and asks for permission.
  4. You approve. Work starts only after this step.
  5. Contractor attends and repairs or advises.
  6. The approved invoice is entered in PayProp and deducted from the next rent.

Real emergencies, such as a suspected gas leak, are never held up waiting for approval. See the emergency guidance. Emergency handling for each plan is set out in your management agreement.

Questions about the plans

Switching terms are set out in your written management agreement.

It can be, because work only starts once you approve it. Quick replies keep things moving, and genuine emergencies are handled under a narrowly defined emergency exception.
